data.hypothesis: A factor-two target tile retains source-register reuse while halving the per-thread force accumulators compared with the valid but slower factor-four parent. With 256 threads, 512 outputs per block preserves the two-target mapping. This may reduce register-pressure or occupancy costs, but requires official measurement; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: The supplied measurements are relevant to this target-axis coarsening path; they do not establish why the factor-four candidate was slower.
memory_lessons.claim: The factor-four candidate was correct but had a measured mean of 0.004442 s and score 0.2937, versus the supplied baseline mean of 0.001847 s and score 0.5. A smaller coarsening factor is a useful distinct experiment, not a guaranteed improvement.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this factor-two candidate with the full correctness suite and official timing metric, then compare it to both the factor-four parent and baseline.

data.notes: The factor-four parent and baseline comparisons are supplied controller measurements; no factor-two result or register/occupancy data is available yet. The kernel streams sources from global memory without shared-memory staging, preserves each target's source iteration order and mass, and bounds-checks both outputs for tail blocks. The controller should run correctness and official timing.
transformations: Change per-thread target coarsening from four outputs to two, with target indices separated by blockDim.x.
Set items_per_block to 512 for 256-thread blocks so each thread covers two logical outputs.
Stream each source particle once per loop iteration and reuse its position and mass across valid target accumulators.
Bounds-check both target indices and store each valid output exactly once; keep shared_memory_bytes at zero.
